On Mon, Mar 22, 2026 at 09:24, rohan_mehta@redwood.com wrote:
> Laura, Marissa — can you own triage and confirm whether we should flip traffic to the compatible variant ...

Preliminary findings (first 30m):
- Root cause signal: increased KV cache miss rate due to suffix cache eviction triggered by a recent config change (batching window increased from 20ms => 50ms last night for all tenants).
- Secondary factor: the fallback path to the CPU-encoded variant has higher per-request latency; in combination with cache misses this amplified end-to-end latency and led to overload and 5xxs on the model pool.
- Impact: Peak error rate ~11% at 08:56 PST; p95 token latency ~1.4s. Throughput dropped ~32% for checkout route.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- Rolled back batching window to 20ms for SilverLedge's routing policy (ROLLBACK ID: rb-20260322-01).
- Scaled the dedicated pool +2 GPU capacity as an emergency burst (manual override).

Attached: incident log excerpt and tracer spans (silverledge_incident_log_excerpt.zip). Next 1h actions: continue trace correlation, validate rollbacks, and prepare formal timeline/IR.

— Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Redwood

Subject: SilverLedge impact — summary, short-term remediation and proposed commercial remedy

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the patience this morning; quick executive summary + what we're delivering by EOD:

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-03-22 08:40 — 09:10 PST (primary surge), residual increased p95 through 09:40 while autoscale converged.
- Symptoms: elevated 5xxs (~11% peak), p95 token latency increased to ~1.4s, throughput reduced ~32% on checkout route.
- Root cause (prelim): cross-tenant batching-window config change increased KV eviction pressure for SilverLedge's hot keyspace, which amplified fallback path latency and produced overload on the dedicated pool.

Deliverables (short-term, by EOD):
1) Completed timeline and evidence bundle (attached) — includes tracer spans and config diff.
2) Immediate config policy: isolate SilverLedge routing policy from global batching changes (implemented).
3) Stability measure: permanent guardrails to prevent global batching window flips without canary and tenant-level opt-out.
4) Commercial remedy: proposed credit of 15% of March hosted usage (to be finalized after damage assessment).

Attachments: sla_summary_q2.pdf, mitigation_playbook-draft.md (both attached in this thread).

We propose a short readout call tomorrow to walk through the timeline and longer-term fixes. Marissa will schedule.

— Rishi Malhotra
VP, Customer Success & Commercials
Redwood Inference
